1.w: The prayer of an oppressed man, as he grows faint and pours out his lament before the Lord . O Lord , hear my prayer. Pay attention to my cry for help.

2.w: Do not ignore me in my time of trouble. Listen to me. When I call out to you, quickly answer me.

3.w: For my days go up in smoke, and my bones are charred as in a fireplace.

4.w: My heart is parched and withered like grass, for I am unable to eat food.

5.w: Because of the anxiety that makes me groan, my bones protrude from my skin.

6.w: I am like an owl in the wilderness; I am like a screech owl among the ruins.

7.w: I stay awake; I am like a solitary bird on a roof.

8.w: All day long my enemies taunt me; those who mock me use my name in their curses.

9.w: For I eat ashes as if they were bread, and mix my drink with my tears,

10.w: because of your anger and raging fury. Indeed, you pick me up and throw me away.

11.w: My days are coming to an end, and I am withered like grass.

12.w: But you, O Lord , rule forever, and your reputation endures.

13.w: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion. For it is time to have mercy on her, for the appointed time has come.

14.w: Indeed, your servants take delight in her stones and feel compassion for the dust of her ruins.

15.w: The nations will respect the reputation of the Lord , and all the kings of the earth will respect his splendor

16.w: when the Lord rebuilds Zion and reveals his splendor,

17.w: when he responds to the prayer of the destitute and does not reject their request.

18.w: The account of his intervention will be recorded for future generations; people yet to be born will praise the Lord .

19.w: For he will look down from his sanctuary above; from heaven the Lord will look toward earth,

20.w: in order to hear the painful cries of the prisoners and to set free those condemned to die,

21.w: so they may proclaim the name of the Lord in Zion and praise him in Jerusalem

22.w: when the nations gather together, and the kingdoms pay tribute to the Lord .

23.w: He has taken away my strength in the middle of life; he has cut short my days.

24.w: I say, “O my God, please do not take me away in the middle of my life. You endure through all generations.

25.w: In earlier times you established the earth; the skies are your handiwork.

26.w: They will perish, but you will endure. They will wear out like a garment; like clothes you will remove them and they will disappear.

27.w: But you remain; your years do not come to an end.

28.w: The children of your servants will settle down here, and their descendants will live securely in your presence.”
